subject: Blackbird deployment — forced model + region lock request
messages:
From: John Sullivan <john.sullivan@healthcareco.com>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Blackbird rollout — hard requirement: EU-only + no-fallback to smaller models

Monica,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick clarification from our security/compliance team: for the initial Blackbird integration (prod config) we must have two guarantees before we go live:

1) All inference must terminate in the EU region (no cross-region failover).
2) If the primary model (blackbird-1) is unavailable, we do NOT want automatic fallback to any smaller or different model. Instead the request should fail explicitly so we can surface an incident to our app and run our own mitigation.

This is non-negotiable for our auditors — they view silent model substitution as a data control and model provenance issue. We are prepared to accept a slightly higher cost (reserved capacity + dedicated pool) if it lets us keep deterministic model behavior.

I've attached a short PDF with the compliance note from our security director. Can you confirm whether Redwood can enforce a forced-model + region lock for HCC production and what the technical/commercial implications are?

Best,
John Sullivan
VP Product, Healthcare Co
john.sullivan@healthcareco.com

Forwarding John from Healthcare Co — they are requesting a strict configuration: region lock to EU and NO automatic fallback to alternate models. They explicitly want requests to fail (so they can control incident handling) if the primary model isn't available.

Attachments: HCC-SLA-blackbird-req.pdf (customer compliance note)

Can infra/engineering confirm if we can implement a per-customer policy that enforces: 1) region=eu only, 2) force_model=blackbird-1, 3) disable-fallback=true? Also flag any risks/required infra changes and an estimate for timeline and cost. Karthik — please flag if this changes commercialization (reserved capacity ask). Lauren — can product sign off on making this an exception for HCC?

Thanks — Monica

Subject: Re: Fwd: Blackbird rollout — hard requirement: EU-only + no-fallback to smaller models

Monica / team,

Technical summary and constraints: we can implement a per-tenant routing policy with the requested semantics, but there are three important caveats:

- Capacity/availability: To guarantee "fail instead of fallback" semantics, the customer must be on a Dedicated pool bound to blackbird-1 in the EU. If primary nodes are saturated or down, requests will return errors (we can surface 503/504 or a custom 5xx with a clear code). That behavior is already supported in principle, but we need an orchestration change to prevent automatic routing to compatible variants.

- Runtime change: The serving runtime currently has a fallback preference list that is evaluated server-side. We will add a per-tenant flag (force_model: "blackbird-1") that short-circuits fallback. Implementation effort: 2 sprints (3 weeks) for code + e2e tests, plus 1 week for infra rollout in EU. I filed INF-4721 to track this change.

- Edge cases: KV cache warmup and QPS spikes — without fallback, you risk P99 increases and hard failures. Recommended mitigation: reserved warmup nodes + autoscale buffer for first 30 days. Estimated incremental cost: ~30-45% on top of baseline for reserved capacity at launch, then 15-20% ongoing.

Action items I need from AE/legal: a written amendment to the SLA that documents "no-fallback" behavior and acceptable error codes. Also confirmation that the customer accepts the risk profile (i.e., fails over to their app).

I can spin up a proof-of-concept in our EU dev pool this week to validate the force_model flag if we get approval.

— Dev
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving
dev_patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Team,

From a commercial perspective this maps cleanly to a Dedicated / Reserved commitment. If we can guarantee the fixed capacity in the EU and add the "no-fallback" flag, we should be able to secure the HCC deal (deal id HCC-9423). My thoughts:

- Offer: 12-month reserved pool (EU) sized for their 99th percentile QPS, with a market-aligned discount (15% off list) in exchange for the operational constraints.
- Legal: they will need an amendment that spells out the failure modes and our liability cap for forced-model configurations.
- Timeline: customer wants prod by mid-April. Dev estimate puts the infra change at ~4 weeks — we need to fast-track the INF-4721 ticket and prioritize capacity provisioning.

I can present this to the customer tomorrow if we get a confirm from product/engineering and a draft amendment from legal.

— Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Blackbird rollout — hard requirement: EU-only + no-fallback to smaller models

Thanks all — I agree we can treat this as an exception for HCC under the following conditions:

1) Dedicated EU pool is provisioned and reserved for HCC (no multi-tenant sharing for blackbird-1).
2) Product will add the per-tenant flag (force_model=\"blackbird-1\" and disable_fallback=true). Dev to target an expedited 3-week run: 2 sprints of engineering + 1 week infra rollout. Track under INF-4721.
3) Legal to provide an SLA amendment and an explicit acceptance from the customer acknowledging the risk of hard failures and the error-code contract (we will return 524 for forced-model unavailable).
4) Security to review and sign off on the EU-only routing configuration (no cross-region KV replication for this tenant).

Monica / Karthik: please capture the offer in a short one-pager for the customer (capacity, price delta, timeline, and acceptance signature). Legal: please prepare a draft amendment and loop in security/compliance. Dev: start work on a PoC in EU dev pool once legal confirms amendment language.

I'll approve prioritization for INF-4721 — we need the business to close.

— Lauren
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
